framework.name: National Standards for Family and Consumer Sciences Education (NASAFACS 3.0), with Illinois Learning Standards for the K-5 units
framework.note: Codes are NASAFACS area-of-study content standards (FCS 8.2 = food safety and sanitation, etc.), plus Illinois Physical Development & Health, Mathematics and Social Science standards for the K-5 units; alignment is the course author's judgment, not a certification.

standards.text: Carry out food safety and sanitation procedures in a kitchen.
Judge the factors that affect food safety from production through consumption.
Apply risk-management steps to food safety and sanitation.
Select, use and maintain kitchen equipment according to accepted standards.
Select, use and maintain kitchen tools and equipment safely and correctly.
Use professional food preparation methods and techniques to produce food products.
Follow food safety and sanitation procedures while handling tools and food.
Use standard food preparation techniques, including accurate measuring, to follow a recipe.
Apply menu-planning principles built on standardized recipes.
Acquire, handle and use foods to meet nutrition and wellness needs.
Show the skills needed to produce, alter or repair apparel and textile products.
Show basic textile and apparel design and construction skills.
Select, use and care for tools according to accepted standards.
Construct, alter or repair textile products using appropriate equipment and techniques.
Apply apparel and textile design skills in a made product.
Show transferable and employability skills such as safe equipment use and following procedures.
Evaluate fibers, fabrics and textile materials for their properties and uses.
Use fashion, apparel and textile design skills, including reading and using patterns.
Apply construction skills to produce a textile product from a pattern.
Manage individual and family resources such as clothing.
Use professional cooking methods and techniques across menu categories.
Use and maintain cooking equipment safely and to industry standards.
Handle and prepare foods in ways that support nutrition and wellness.
Apply food safety practices, including safe cooking temperatures.
Evaluate the nutritional needs of individuals and families across the life span.
Plan, acquire and prepare foods that meet nutrition and wellness needs.
Analyze factors that influence nutrition and wellness practices.
Apply menu-planning principles and techniques to meet needs.
Evaluate nutrition principles, food plans and preparation techniques.
Evaluate nutrition principles and food preparation techniques through the science behind them.
Evaluate how science and technology influence food, nutrition and wellness.
Apply food preparation techniques with an understanding of how ingredients react.
Apply food safety and food testing procedures.
Analyze principles of human growth and development across the life span.
Analyze conditions that influence a child's growth and development.
Provide a safe and healthy environment for children in one's care.
Evaluate caregiving practices that support children's growth and development.
Use techniques that build positive, collaborative relationships with children.
Manage financial resources to meet personal and family goals across the life span.
Manage individual and family resources such as food, shelter, transportation and time.
Analyze strategies to manage multiple roles and responsibilities.
Analyze relationships between the economic system and consumer choices.
Plan a menu using standardized recipes to meet a stated need.
Produce food products using professional preparation methods.
Manage resources such as money, time and materials to complete a project.
Show teamwork and leadership skills while carrying out a shared task.
Demonstrate employability skills such as planning, costing and finishing work.
Practice basic sanitation, beginning with proper hand washing.
Recognize how clean hands and surfaces keep food safe.
Identify ways to promote health and prevent illness, such as hand washing.
Show strategies that prevent the spread of disease, including cleanliness.
Follow basic kitchen safety rules for hot, cold and sharp things.
Use simple kitchen tools safely and put them away properly.
Identify dangerous situations and safe ways to respond to them.
Describe safety methods for handling hazards at home and in the kitchen.
Recognize what foods the body needs to grow and stay well.
Identify what influences the food choices people make.
Identify healthy actions, such as a good diet, that help the body work well.
Tell positive from negative effects of food and health choices on the body.
Show teamwork and take responsibility for a shared job.
Practice work-readiness habits such as following steps and finishing a task.
Use time and materials responsibly to get a job done.
Measure ingredients accurately as part of following a recipe.
Handle and prepare foods correctly using simple recipes.
Measure length by choosing and using the right tool.
Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses using standard units.
Use basic hand-sewing skills to repair an item, such as sewing on a button.
Practice simple textile construction skills with a needle and thread.
Use sharp tools safely and store them correctly.
Make simple money decisions such as saving, spending and comparing prices.
Manage resources like money and belongings by making choices.
Explain that people make choices because they cannot have everything they want.
Show how our choices affect ourselves and others in positive and negative ways.
Solve money problems using dollars, quarters, dimes, nickels and pennies.
Keep hands, food and work areas clean before, during and after cooking.
Prepare a simple food by following the steps of a recipe.
Plan and prepare a simple food that meets a nutrition need.
Work as a team to plan, cook and clean up.
Use safe practices when working around kitchen hazards.
